theater: 雅典城邦與伯羅奔尼撒半島

battle.name: 伯羅奔尼撒戰爭
battle.theater: 雅典城邦與伯羅奔尼撒半島
battle.brief: 公元前431年雅典聯盟與斯巴達聯盟開戰，歷二十七年，公元前404年雅典投降。陸戰靠重步兵方陣，海戰靠三列槍戰船；卡面這支兩米長、槍尾帶銅套的斯巴達長矛正是方陣核心，公元前425年斯巴達重步兵在斯法克特里亞島灘頭覆滅，公元前405年伊奧斯波塔米海戰後雅典被圍至斷糧。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元前431年至前404年、雅典海上帝國與斯巴達伯羅奔尼撒同盟之間的一場希臘內戰，戰場橫跨希臘本島、愛琴海、小亞細亞西岸與西西里島。雅典一方是提洛同盟的盟主：以雅典城為基地的公民重步兵方陣，加上數百艘三列槍戰船構成的海上帝國，盟邦按約按年向雅典交納貢金，戰事由十人將軍委員會（從五百人議事會中選出）逐人輪任執掌，議事會與陪審法庭掌握財政與外交。斯巴達一方是伯羅奔尼撒同盟的盟主：五王制與長老院並存的公民制國家，重步兵方陣的戰鬥名聲遠揚於歐洲，但海軍薄弱，官方船隊不過數百艘，多數戰役只派出一部分公民兵作戰，其餘由盟邦兵分擔。雙方都不是純粹的希臘人國家，戰爭也牽入波斯：居魯士二世以金銀資助斯巴達的海軍，後來又倒向雅典；西西里方面，敘拉古主導的西西里聯盟與迦太基結盟，赫爾墨克拉底率領的敘拉古軍與斯巴達援軍指揮官基利波斯一起對抗聯軍，迦太基的戰艦與僱傭兵亦參與其中。另有科林斯、邁奧尼尼亞、埃利斯與色雷斯的城邦站在斯巴達一邊，雅典則以薩摩斯、米利都與愛奧尼亞的航線為核心。因此這是一場以兩套聯盟體系為骨架，卻被三方財力與海運牽動的長期消耗戰。
countriesEn: The war was a Greek civil war fought between the Athenian maritime empire and the Peloponnesian League led by Sparta from 431 to 404 BC, across the Greek mainland, the Aegean, the western coast of Asia Minor and Sicily. The Athenian side was the hegemon of the Delian League: a phalanx of citizen heavy infantry based on the city of Athens, supported by several hundred triremes that made the empire a sea power. The subject cities paid annual tribute to Athens, and war was directed by a board of ten strategoi, elected in rotation from the Council of Five Hundred, while the Assembly and the jury courts handled finance and foreign policy. The Spartan side was the hegemon of the Peloponnesian League: a dual-kingdom citizen state with a council of elders, famous throughout Europe for its heavy infantry phalanx but short of warships, its official fleet numbering only a few hundred hulls, and it normally sent only a fraction of its citizen army on campaign, leaving the rest of the burden to the allies. Neither camp was purely Greek, and Persia was drawn in: Cyrus the Younger paid for the Spartan navy with silver and gold before switching his support to the Athenians; in the west, Syracuse led the Sicilian coalition with Carthaginian backing, with the Syracusan forces under Hermocrates and the Spartan commander Gylippus facing the coalition, and Carthaginian warships and hired troops taking part. Corinth, Megara, Elis and the Chalcidian cities stood with Sparta, while Athens led through Samos, Miletus and the shipping lanes of Ionia. The result was a war of attrition built on the skeleton of two alliance systems, but pulled about by the money and the sea lanes of three wider powers.
people: 雅典方面的關鍵人物是伯里克利。他在前428年以前連續擔任將軍，主張以城牆與海軍應戰：斯巴達人燒田，雅典就用錢不用兵，等對方在伯羅奔尼撒平原上因缺糧而自行退去。這套方針被前430年的疫病打斷——瘟疫在雅典城邦、波提狄亞與雅典軍中同時蔓延，伯里克利本人感染後在次年去世，死前留下那段著名的葬禮演說。尼西亞斯是反對遠征的溫和派將軍，也是前415年西西里遠征的主帥之一，堅持反對出兵，最後死於撤退途中的海戰；亞西比德年輕而雄辯，是遠征計畫的推動者，卻在出征途中被召回，後來叛逃投波斯，在小亞細亞策反、促成和約，回師後一度掌權，最終再度出走。克里昂以平民派首領的身分推行對斯巴達的強硬政策，力主經營皮洛斯，後在安菲波利斯陣亡。斯巴達方面最耀眼的是布里西達斯：他以大膽率領數千名重步兵跨越科林斯地峽，攻入色雷斯的安菲波利斯，奪城後又策劃向雅典的盟邦進攻，最後在安菲波利斯城外陣亡，雅典的封地就此易手。海戰的關鍵是呂西安德，他用波斯人的錢造出數百艘戰艦，在伊奧斯波塔米迫使雅典投降，隨後又在米利都強行奪取財物。敘拉古方面由赫爾墨克拉底主導外交與戰局，而敘拉古議會中反對向西西里用兵的聲音，也迫使雅典改變了遠征計畫。
peopleEn: The key figure on the Athenian side was Pericles, who served as general continuously until 428 BC and argued for meeting Sparta behind the walls and the fleet: when the Spartans burned the crops, Athens would spend money rather than men and wait for the enemy to withdraw from the Peloponnese for want of provisions. That line of policy was broken by the plague that struck in 430 BC and spread through the city, through Potidaea and through the Athenian army; Pericles caught the disease himself and died the following year, leaving behind the funeral speech that bears his name. Nicias, the cautious general, opposed the Sicilian venture, served as one of its commanders and died in the naval action of the retreat. Alcibiades, young and eloquent, drove the expedition forward, was recalled from the command while the fleet was still en route, and later fled to Persian service, working to subvert Athenian allies in Asia Minor and to bring about the peace; he returned to lead the city and finally exiled himself again. Cleon, leader of the popular party, pursued a hard line against Sparta, insisted on holding Pylos, and was killed at Amphipolis. The most conspicuous Spartan was Brasidas, who with sheer daring led several thousand hoplites across the Isthmus of Corinth into Chalcidice, took Amphipolis and then planned an advance on the Athenian allies, only to be killed outside the city, which handed the Athenian possession over to Sparta. At sea the decisive figure was Lysander, who built several hundred triremes with Persian money, forced Athens to surrender after Aegospotami, and then stripped Miletus of its wealth. On the Syracusan side Hermocrates directed diplomacy and strategy, while the Syracusan assembly's resistance to sending more troops westward was itself one of the factors that changed the Athenian plan.
kits: 卡面這支斯巴達長矛是重步兵方陣的骨幹：兩米長的木杆，前端裝金屬矛頭，槍尾有銅套並帶尖錐，行軍時可插在地上支撐身體，列陣時可架在肩上形成遮蔽，進抵短兵距離後才以矛尖刺擊。與它配合的是圓盾（aspis），直徑近一米的木胎圓盾，邊緣包青銅或鐵，盾面可供身後的同袍搭手遮護；再加上科林斯式或開放面式的頭盔、胸甲、脛甲、短劍，以及每人兩支的投擲標槍。斯巴達重步兵另有佩爾隆邦式重裝胸甲與短劍作近戰備用。遠征與攻城期間，兩軍都大量使用投射武器：陶製與木製的投石機、投石索手，攻城用的撞槌與土坡。西西里線上，敘拉古造出大型攻城機械與高塔，用以對付雅典城牆；斯巴達在狄刻利亞設長期圍城據點，並以石彈投擲器攻擊雅典的防禦工事。海戰的技術核心是三列槍戰船：下層划槳手分三列，船首裝青銅撞角，船尾有可抬起的船尾柱與登陸跳板。實物證據也對得上：2011年至2012年在皮洛斯南坡發掘的戰士墳場，埋有約一千五百具遺骸與大量白蠟木矛桿，與文獻所載長矛相符；科林斯海岸的水下考古亦出水過青銅矛頭與銅套。卡面兵器正是這套裝備中被後世視為希臘公民戰士標誌的那一件。
kitsEn: The dory on the card is the backbone of the hoplite phalanx: a wooden shaft about two metres long with a metal head at the front and a bronze ferrule and spike at the rear, which could be planted in the ground to support the man on the march, shouldered in the ranks to form a roof of points, and driven home only after the line had closed to spear range. It worked with the aspis, a round wooden shield nearly a metre across with a bronze or iron rim, whose face gave shelter to the man behind; and with a Corinthian or open-faced helmet, a cuirass, greaves, the short sword, and the pair of throwing javelins each man carried. Spartan heavy infantry also had the corselet and the short sword for close work. Over long campaigns and sieges both sides used missile weapons extensively: pottery and timber stone-throwers, slingers, battering rams and earthen ramps. In the Sicilian theatre Syracuse built large siege engines and tall towers against the Athenian walls; Sparta established a permanent blockade base at Decelea and used stone-throwers against the Athenian defences. At sea the technical core was the trireme, with rowers arranged on three levels, a bronze ram at the bow and a liftable sternpost and boarding bridge at the back. The physical evidence matches: the warrior cemetery excavated on the southern slope of Pylos in 2011 and 2012 held some fifteen hundred individuals together with large numbers of ash spear shafts, consistent with the written sources, and underwater work off Corinth has produced bronze spearheads and ferrules. The weapon on the card is precisely the piece that later ages took as the emblem of the Greek citizen soldier.
tactics: 斯巴達的打法是陸軍方陣的正面壓制：重步兵肩並肩排成數層縱深，右翼的兵種依次為重裝兵、精銳輕裝兵與射手，擊潰對手右翼後再捲入中央。斯巴達的徵兵制度決定了戰役節奏：公民兵按戶籍輪值，遠征多在夏季，出兵常只及全部公民兵的三分之一，國內隨時可能被敵人偷襲；這種一年一役、規模受限的作戰方式，使雙方陷入消耗而非決戰。雅典的對策是避免陸上會戰，以城牆、海軍與錢財周旋，斯巴達則因缺糧退回伯羅奔尼撒；前413年斯巴達在狄刻利亞建立長期據點，切斷雅典鄉間收入與勞里翁銀礦，海軍優勢的意義被大幅削弱。前425年皮洛斯的守軍德摩斯梯尼在夜間率重步兵登陸斯法克特里亞島，狹窄灘頭使斯巴達方陣無法展開，雅典軍自三面夾擊，斯巴達軍覆滅，兩百九十二人繳械投降。前415年雅典派出數百艘戰艦與數萬人的海陸大軍進攻西西里，卻在遠征途中被召回主帥，又在外交上失誤，最後在敘拉古大港被封鎖夜襲，海軍損失過半，撤退時遭追擊殲滅。最終決戰在公元前405年的伊奧斯波塔米：雅典戰士離船取水，斯巴達海軍在海峽狹窄處衝鋒，摧毀停在岸邊的雅典艦隊，數千名登岸者被殺、被俘，雅典城隨之被封鎖至斷糧而降。
tacticsEn: The Spartan method was frontal pressure of the infantry phalanx: heavy infantry stood shoulder to shoulder in several ranks, the right wing being formed in order of heavy troops, elite light troops and slingers, so that breaking the enemy right could roll the whole line; and the Spartan manning system decided the rhythm of the war. Citizen troops were levied by household rotation, campaigns were fought in the summer, and only about a third of the citizen army normally went out, leaving the homeland open to a counter-stroke. That annual and limited scale turned the war into an attritional contest rather than a single decisive clash. Athens sought to avoid battle on land and to fight behind walls, fleet and treasury, and Sparta withdrew into the Peloponnese for want of provisions; in 413 BC Sparta fortified Decelea, cutting off the rural revenues of Attica and the silver of the Laurium mines and greatly reducing the value of Athenian sea power. In 425 BC Demosthenes landed hoplites at night on Sphacteria, where the narrow beach denied the Spartan phalanx room to deploy; the Athenians attacked from three sides, the Spartan force was destroyed, and two hundred and ninety-two men laid down their arms. In 415 BC Athens sent a vast army and fleet to Sicily, but recalled her commanders on the way and stumbled in her diplomacy; finally she was shut up in the great harbour of Syracuse, where a night attack destroyed half the fleet and the retreat was hunted down. The last decision came at Aegospotami in 405 BC: the Athenian crews were ashore for water when the Spartan squadron charged in the narrows and smashed the fleet lying at anchor, killing those on shore and capturing the rest, and Athens was then sealed in and starved into surrender.
data: 兵力與損失有較可靠的數字可引。前431年斯巴達入侵阿提卡時，聯軍約有三萬重步兵與相若數目的輕裝兵；前413年駐紮狄刻利亞的斯巴達軍約二萬重步兵。雅典方面，伯里克利自述可用重步兵約一萬三千人（公民與外邦人居所合計），城內常備三列槍戰船約一百艘，戰事高峰時船數增至二百艘以上。前430年雅典瘟疫，修昔底德估計約四分之一至三分之一的人口死於疫病，後人依他記錄的年度死亡人數推算，雅典城內死者約四千四百人。前415年西西里遠征，雅典出動戰艦約一百五十艘、兵力約四萬人；敘拉古一方可集合重步兵與其他西西里城邦的援軍共數萬，並在戰役中造出六十餘艘新船。結果是雅典損失慘重，約五千至六千人陣亡、七千名俘虜死於敘拉古的采石坑，最後逃回者不足兩千。前425年斯法克特里亞島，斯巴達軍大部被殲，僅二百九十二名重步兵投降。前405年伊奧斯波塔米海戰，雅典不足百艘的艦隊損失殆盡，約四千人當場被殺，約七千人被俘，隨後在雅典投降後遭殺害。前404年雅典陷落，長城被拆，城市的居民大批逃亡。全戰爭歷時二十七年，其間有一段前421年尼西亞斯和約劃出的間歇期。
dataEn: A few figures can be stated with some confidence. In the invasion of Attica in 431 BC the Spartan coalition mustered about thirty thousand hoplites with a comparable number of light troops, and the force that garrisoned Decelea in 413 BC was about twenty thousand hoplites. On the Athenian side Pericles claimed some thirteen thousand hoplites available, citizens and metics together, and about a hundred triremes in the city, with the fleet growing past two hundred at the height of the fighting. The plague that struck Athens in 430 BC killed, on Thucydides' estimate, between a quarter and a third of the population, and later reconstruction from the annual figures he records puts Athenian deaths in the city at roughly forty-four hundred. The Sicilian expedition of 415 BC sent about a hundred and fifty triremes and some forty thousand men; Syracuse could raise heavy infantry and the aid of the other Sicilian cities in the tens of thousands and built more than sixty new ships during the campaign. The result was ruin: perhaps five or six thousand Athenians were killed, seven thousand prisoners died in the stone quarries of Syracuse, and fewer than two thousand got home. At Sphacteria in 425 BC the Spartan garrison was destroyed almost to the last man, only two hundred and ninety-two hoplites surrendering. At Aegospotami in 405 BC the Athenian fleet of fewer than a hundred sail was lost, about four thousand men were killed on the spot and some seven thousand were captured and afterwards executed after the surrender. In 404 BC Athens fell, the Long Walls were pulled down, and the city emptied of much of its population. The whole war lasted twenty-seven years, interrupted by the truce of Nicias in 421 BC.
cause: 直接起因是一連串邊境與海上糾紛。前433年科基拉與其母邦科林斯決鬥，雅典出手援助科基拉並迫使科林斯退讓，海上霸權的爭奪由此升溫。前432年，科林斯的殖民地波提狄亞在雅典的壓力下倒向斯巴達同盟，科林斯派兵駐守不肯撤退，斯巴達的仲裁請求又讓聯盟內部的裂痕擴大。前431年，雅典頒布梅加里亞法令，把曾經的盟友排除在帝國的市場與港口之外，愛琴海商路被切斷，斯巴達聯盟的怨氣集中爆發。深層原因是實力對比：斯巴達自居希臘領袖，要求各城邦自治，卻要靠同盟的軍力維持霸權；雅典的帝國其實是一套以貢金與海軍維持的強制秩序。雙方的結盟宣誓，以及以解放為名的號召，令開戰在聯盟內部也得到響應。前431年三月末底比斯人夜襲普拉提亞，四月斯巴達聯軍越過地峽進入阿提卡，戰爭全面爆發。
causeEn: The immediate causes were a chain of frontier and sea disputes. In 433 BC Corcyra fought its mother city Corinth, Athens intervened on Corcyra's side and forced Corinth to give way, and the struggle over sea power sharpened. In 432 BC the Corinthian colony of Potidaea, pressed by Athens, turned to the Spartan alliance; Corinth kept a garrison there and refused to withdraw, and Sparta's request for arbitration widened the cracks inside the coalition. In 431 BC Athens issued the Megarian Decree, excluding a former ally from the markets and harbours of the empire, cutting the Corinthian trade routes, and the accumulated grievances of the Spartan alliance came to a head. The deeper cause was the balance of power: Sparta claimed the leadership of Greece and the freedom of the cities while enforcing its own hegemony through the alliance, whereas the Athenian empire was really a system of compulsion maintained by tribute and by the fleet. The oaths sworn on both sides, and the cry of liberation that accompanied them, meant that the outbreak drew support from within the alliances as well. In the last days of March 431 the Thebans attacked Plataea by night; in April the Spartan coalition crossed the Isthmus into Attica and the war began in earnest.
impact: 這場戰爭的結果被後世視為古典城邦時代的終點。雅典的海上帝國解體，貢金收入消失，長城被拆，雅典從霸權者變成斯巴達的附庸；但斯巴達隨即面對自己無法治理的廣闊屬地與反覆的背叛，公元前404年之後開啟的科林斯戰爭（公元前395年至前387年）最終以國王和約收場，斯巴達霸權崩解，霸權先後落到底比斯，再落到馬其頓的腓力二世手中，公元前338年喀羅尼亞一戰後，希臘城邦的獨立幾乎全部終結，而這一切的起點正是雅典與斯巴達的這一場消耗。在思想與文學上，修昔底德留下的《伯羅奔尼撒戰爭史》示範了以證據重建過去的方法，把恐懼揭示為強權政治的真實動機；米利都對話與西西里遠征的演說，把強者權力與正義之間的落差寫成永恆難題，後世的國際關係與國際法至今仍在此基礎上討論。軍事上，這是一場把重步兵方陣推到極致的戰爭，長矛與圓盾的配合被視為公民平等與勇氣的象徵，斯巴達的武力神話從此既榮譽又負債，最終在西西里與小亞細亞的消耗中反噬自己。
impactEn: The outcome of this war is commonly taken as the end of the classical city-state. The Athenian maritime empire was dissolved, the tribute stopped, the Long Walls came down, and Athens changed from hegemon to subject of Sparta; but Sparta then faced territories it could not govern and allies it could not trust, and the Corinthian War that followed 404 BC ended in the King's Peace and the collapse of Spartan hegemony. Power passed to Thebes and then to Macedon, and after Chaeronea in 338 BC the independence of the Greek city-states was effectively over, with this war of exhaustion as the starting point. Intellectually and in literature, Thucydides' History of the Peloponnesian War demonstrated the reconstruction of the past from evidence and exposed fear as the true motive of strong-power politics; the Melian Dialogue and the Sicilian speeches turned the gap between might and right into a permanent problem, and modern international relations and law still argue from that ground. Militarily the war pushed the hoplite phalanx to its limit, and the pairing of long spear and round shield became the emblem of citizen equality and courage, so that the Spartan martial reputation, once an honour, became a liability and finally consumed the state in the attritional fighting in Sicily and Asia Minor.
result: 結果分三段。前431至前421年首輪交鋒以和約收場，尼西亞斯和約劃出間歇期，斯巴達保住伯羅奔尼撒，雅典保住城牆與帝國框架；但和約條件互相矛盾，阿爾戈斯同盟破裂，前418年曼丁納之戰再由斯巴達取勝。前415至前413年的西西里遠征是戰局的轉折，雅典投入主力卻全軍覆沒，損失的遠征軍、戰艦與財政餘裕再也補不回來，此後雅典再無力與斯巴達正面爭雄。前414年起斯巴達在狄刻利亞建立長期圍城線，前410年基齊庫斯之役重創波斯援軍，前406年諾提翁海戰中雅典海軍被徹底殲滅，前405年伊奧斯波塔米海戰決定一切：呂西安德的艦隊摧毀雅典最後的海軍，雅典被封鎖，城市因饑荒與疫病而崩潰，公元前404年三月至四月議會派出代表談判，雅典人交出長城與殘餘戰艦，接受斯巴達的霸權，三十人寡頭隨後清洗民主派。全戰爭以雅典投降告終，斯巴達取得勝利，卻在兩代之內被自身的擴張拖累。
resultEn: The outcome came in three stages. The first round of fighting, 431 to 421 BC, ended in a truce, the Peace of Nicias, which left Sparta the Peloponnese and Athens its walls and the framework of its empire; but the terms contradicted each other, the Argive alliance broke down, and the Spartan victory at Mantinea in 418 BC followed. The Sicilian expedition of 415 to 413 BC was the turning point: Athens had committed its main force and lost it entire, and the men, ships and financial margin it had spent could never be replaced, leaving Athens unable to contest Sparta on equal terms. From 414 BC the Spartans held the permanent blockade line at Decelea; the Athenian victory at Cyzicus in 410 BC wrecked the Persian relieving force; the Athenian fleet was destroyed at Notium in 406 BC; and the battle of Aegospotami in 405 BC settled everything. Lysander's squadron destroyed the last Athenian fleet, Athens was sealed in and starved, and in March and April of 404 BC envoys went out to negotiate: the Athenians gave up the Long Walls and their remaining ships and accepted Spartan hegemony, after which the Thirty settled accounts with the democracy. The war ended in the surrender of Athens and a Spartan victory, and within two generations the victors were being worn down by the very expansion they had won.
